summary: Steel fire tower on Gilman Peak in Chino Hills State Park; State Parks dates it to 1935 (register says 1937), closed 1967, gone today.

facts.design: Steel tower with a cab about 14 by 14 feet, perched about 30 feet up (1938 account)
facts.status_note: Closed 1967; still standing and abandoned in July 1982; register says removed after 1966; no removal year found
facts.agency: Orange County Fire Authority and Los Angeles County Fire Department (register); cooperative project with the State Division of Forestry (State Parks)

access.note: Summit lies in Chino Hills State Park; State Parks history says occasional hikers and bikers use the top; no current access rule found

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb; hikers and bikers use the summit area

events.note: State Parks: finished in about six weeks, dedication set for Saturday 21 Sep 1935; LA Times item of 22 Sep 1935 says ceremonies had opened. Register says built 1937.
Harvey George French announced as lookout in July 1936; Buell Castile was first, briefly (State Parks)
Glenn Downer and wife lived in the tower cab; featured in a 1938 Los Angeles Times article
David and Myrtle McKenzie found unconscious in June 1953, apparently from carbon monoxide; David died, Myrtle lived
Closed with Bolero Peak station for lack of State budget funds
Paseo Grande fire broke out in Corona in late October 1967, just east of the closed lookout, and crossed into Orange County
Abandoned tower still standing in July 1982; bottom of metal ladder cut off to discourage climbers

corrections.why: State Parks history says the tower was finished in about six weeks and dedicated on 21 Sep 1935, and a 22 Sep 1935 LA Times item says the ceremonies had opened. The register's 1937 conflicts with this; confidence medium.

corrections.proposed: 1967 closed for lack of budget funds; removal year unknown
corrections.why: No removal year is documented. The tower was closed in 1967 and was still standing and abandoned in July 1982.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says 1937; State Parks history and 1935 newspaper items put the completion and dedication in September 1935. The story uses 1935 and notes the register's year.

Register says Harvey French was first assigned at completion; State Parks says Buell Castile was first, briefly, and French was announced in July 1936. The story follows State Parks and says the accounts differ.

notes_for_editor: Build year and first operator conflict between the register and the State Parks PDF; the story reports both. Removal year is not documented anywhere read, so no removal event is recorded. The 1982 standing date rests on State Parks and a 1982 Chino Champion item as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, not on the newspaper itself. No current site description or access rule found. Used one web search and four page reads. The State Parks PDF is written in the first person by one author and cites newspapers; it is a secondary history hosted on parks.ca.gov, so its dates were weighed against the 1935 newspaper items on the Forest Lookouts page.
